title: Wreckright
summary: At dusk, the wreck belongs to whoever still holds the ground around it.
body: Before the Great Recall, contracts on Tessell were written as asset recovery, lien enforcement and disputed custody. Employers preferred it that way and so did the free companies, because a war has sides and a property dispute has invoices.

An ejected pilot walks home. Shoot the seat and no one will ever hire you again — not out of sentiment, but because everybody on this continent is somebody's future employer, and the pool of people who can drive one of these is smaller every year.

A machine disabled in the field belongs to whoever holds the ground at dusk. Not to whoever killed it, not automatically to whoever was paying, and never to the pilot in the seat. That custom is wreckright. It is crude, legible and older than most surviving title books.

The Recall Authority does not recognise wreckright. Its order says a stolen state root cannot become lawful salvage, however many hands repaired it. Tessell's answer is equally simple: the Compact abandoned the machines, local shops continued them, and no paper owner came home before dark.
